note: Fits the body and the mindset, misses the wallet and the job description. He works on the DCS control system for an oil refinery — a skilled industrial technical role, not a business owner, physician or equivalent — so 'successful' fails as the criterion is written, even though he is plainly capable and has just built his own house. Income also fails on the evidence: he called $6,000 'a significant investment', said 'the price really would be the only thing leaning towards not doing it', and the money is jointly held with his wife on a shared account. The other three hold cleanly. Health is exactly the neglected area and not a crisis — he trained four times a week for four years and dropped it for six months to build a house, gaining fifteen pounds. He is the good-to-great case almost verbatim, asking for 'a little bit more of guidance' at 5'10" and 193 lb with four years of training behind him, and he is the opposite of gym-averse. The pattern worth noting against the corpus is the shape of his objection: he did not say he could not afford it, he said remote coaching is not worth what in-person coaching costs. That is a value test the stated ICP does not screen for at all — it screens for whether someone can pay, not for whether they believe a remote delivery model is worth the money.
